items.title: Delfeayo Marsalis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

ctx.x: I had become not so good a student by that point. Early on, I was a straight-A student, but by the time I got to Berklee, I had an idea what I wanted to do. Berklee was not really the – Berklee’s not a very regimented – no, no. Let me say it a different way. Berklee treats you as an adult. They don’t treat you like a student, like, “You have to do this.” They’re like, whatever you want, we’re here. I think I could have probably benefitted more from a more structured environment, but that was similar to how my…

“Musasha didn’t show up.” It was kind of jive. There was a number of Japanese students coming in. So we would just – who knew? Finally they caught wind of it, and they were like – I’m sure they knew a lot earlier than they cracked down. They just said, well, whatever. But at a certain point they cracked down on us.
